title: fix(update): keep history queue overload from aborting candidate snapshots
body:
Fixes #178059.
Related: #177482 (not claimed fixed; see the investigation note below).

## What Problem This Solves

Updates can abort with `candidate-snapshot-failed` / `SQLite worker queue capacity reached` when advisory snapshot progress outruns the history database.

## User Impact

Snapshot progress stays bounded, and a certified queue refusal for optional history produces a warning while validation continues. Required recovery and terminal receipts, cancellation, revoked authority, and uncertain cleanup remain failures.

The installed updater owns the progress writer. A running 2026.10.4 updater cannot gain this repair by staging a newer candidate. After a verified backup, affected operators must stop their Gateway through its actual owner and use the documented manual package-manager procedure to install a release containing the fix, then run Doctor and verify startup with the same account, prefix, profile, and state paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot parent started a ledger mutation for every notification and joined them without limiting concurrent admission. The existing three-attempt policy only covered worker commit-admission timeouts; canonical broker overload rejected before that policy could run. The snapshot owner now keeps one write in flight and coalesces pending observations to the latest one. The asynchronous ledger owner recognizes certified pre-dispatch overload only for optional steps and uses its existing bookkeeping-skipped outcome. The obsolete concurrent-failure aggregation is removed.

The reported cause of slow storage and the reporter's local updater modification are not independently attributed here. Controlled broker saturation proves the current source failure boundary.

For #177482, current candidate acquisition already processes database families sequentially through consistent online backup. Both the reported target and current source exclude recognized rehearsal-private state from ordinary artifact-preserving copies. The ten-attempt error identifies the artifact-preserving path, but the report omits its final source-change condition and the reduced rehearsal passes. This change does not establish that candidate-startup root cause or bypass consistency checks.

## Evidence

- Isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; no operator state or serving Gateway used.
- Focused tests: snapshot/watchdog 4/4; asynchronous ledger 3/3. A 256-event burst preserves the latest observation without concurrent callbacks; the real broker test occupies all 128 slots and proves optional refusal, required refusal, and terminal persistence after draining.
- Test time in the consumer sweep: new coalescing regression 0.543s; new real-broker regression 1.991s. An earlier unchanged warm-reader ledger test took 46.247s (12.370s in the later sweep). Initial focused file wall times were dominated by shared subprocess transformation; compiler preparation was 191.135s and 339.301s.
- Core, infrastructure-test, and CLI-update-test tsgo passed. Direct oxlint and oxfmt on all touched TypeScript files passed; `git diff --check` passed. The lint wrapper timed out generating unrelated Plugin SDK declarations after 300s, before lint; direct oxlint was used instead.
- Independent Codex review: no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Full `check:changed` / SQLite inventory was not run under the campaign's local gate budget.
- Both new regressions fail on the original production code: 256 concurrent callbacks instead of one, and rejected optional progress after canonical broker overload. The corrected broker negative control fails cleanly without an unawaited assertion. The import-cycle check passed with zero cycles.
- Affected consumers: 215 distinct tests across 16 files passed across the full run and the focused canary recheck. The initial run exposed two canary fixtures that assumed concurrent callbacks. The interrupted-write case now requires exactly two commits and the accepted copying receipt; the unstartable second-callback uncertainty case was removed. All 81 remaining canary tests passed on recheck (43.66s test-file wall, 71.24s wrapper wall); the other 15 files retain their passing results.
- The unchanged CLI ordered-receipt fixtures took 37.591s and 32.587s; the admission-ledger file summed 154.285s of test time. These pre-existing costs are recorded under the campaign exception, without changing timeouts or assertions.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passed in 4m51.3s with isolated HOME/state. It emitted an unrelated advisory Control UI locale diagnostic (Russian locale pair 303.9 KiB against 300 KiB); the build exited 0. No UI, locale, or baseline files changed.
- Live candidate proof: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .artifacts/l1704/live-proof.ts` under disposable `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `TMPDIR`, with alternate state selectors unset and bundled plugins disabled. This called the real candidate validator and held one real worker reply while occupying all 128 broker slots during snapshot progress. Result: one overload warning, 19 progress writes, all 128 accepted writes settled, `status: ok`, `phase: readiness`, and a persisted `succeeded` terminal record. The candidate's own loopback listener used port 54757; `startupz: started (111721ms)` and `readyz: ready (111723ms)`. Whole proof: 127.83s, exit 0. Candidate cleanup stopped the owned Gateway.
- Same isolated environment: `pnpm openclaw update status --json --timeout 1` exited 0 in 15.42s and read back `lastRun.status: succeeded`, `phase: finished`, completed snapshot/startup/cleanup receipts, and ready build artifacts at the PR head. The empty disposable profile has no channel credentials; registry `dev` returned 404 and the one-second Git fetch budget was unverified. These status-inspection limitations do not replace the successful direct readiness probes.
- This is current-source snapshot → Doctor → candidate Gateway readiness proof. It does not claim a published 2026.10.4→2026.10.5 package swap, a live provider inference turn, or reproduction of #177482.

Production LOC: +38/-29 (net +9); tests: +233/-110 (net +123; includes formatter reflow); docs: +11/-1. The small production increase bounds progress and preserves the ledger's existing required/optional distinction without changing broker limits, schemas, dependencies, or options.
